* 3rd Team [[All-American]] by Associated Press (2012-13) }} '''Jeffree David "Jeff" Withey''' (born March 7, 1990, in [[San Diego]], [[California]]) is an [[All-American]] [[Division I (NCAA)]] basketball player for the [[University of Kansas]]. He is projected to be drafted in the [[2013 NBA Draft]] {{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Jeff-Withey-5259/|title=NBA Draft Prospects in the Big 12, Part Three (#11-15)|publisher=DraftExpress LLC |year=2012}}{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/results/players?id=19763&_slug_=jeff-withey&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fnba%2fdraft%2fresults%2fplayers%3fid%3d19763%26_slug_%3djeff-withey|title=NBA DraftTracker: Jeff Withey|year=2012}} and is known for his shot-blocking ability and his defensive presence. ==High school career== ===Horizon High School=== Withey led Horizon High School to the state Division IV title in his sophomore season (2006) {{cite web|url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20061102/news_1s2p-notes.html|title=Horizon 7-footer chooses Louisville for basketball|publisher=Union-Tribune Publishing Co.|year=2006}} and he graduated in the class of 2008.{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=8&c=1&nid=1947382|title=Scout: Jeff Withey|publisher=Microsoft|year=2012}} In the game preceding the state championship game, Withey and his teammates had to face a San Joaquin Memorial team in the Southern California Regional Championship game that featured three seniors who were future NBA players, [[Robin Lopez|Robin]] & [[Brook Lopez]] and [[Quincy Pondexter]]. In a dramatic double overtime game, Withey and his teammates overcame the SJM squad and went on to win the title in the following game.{{cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/contests/mBbA_N82pUy_dtA9VNRnow/basketball-winter-05-06/boxscore-horizon-san-diego-vs-san-joaquin-memorial-fresno.htm|title=Horizon edges San Joaquin Memorial|publisher=Maxpreps|year=2006}} In his senior season he averaged 20.8 points, 13.0 rebounds, and 7.3 blocked shots per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/25/sports/ncaabasketball/jeff-withey-of-kansas-is-a-shot-blocker-supreme.html|title=Kansas Center’s Reach Has Foes Grasping at Straws|publisher=The New York Times Company|year=2012}} ==College career== ===University of Arizona (2008)=== Withey had originally committed to play for Louisville, but switched his commitment to Arizona. Following the resignation of [[Lute Olson]] in October of Withey's freshman season, he decided to transfer from Arizona. He did not see any playing time for the Wildcats during his semester of the 2008-09 season. ===University of Kansas (2009–present)=== Withey transferred to Kansas in January 2009, but was ineligible to play until the end of the 2009 fall semester due to the NCAA transfer rules requiring him to sit out a year. He initially saw limited playing time during the second half of the 2009-10 season and the 2010-11 season, playing behind [[Cole Aldrich]] and the Morris twins. In his [[2011–12 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|junior year]], after twin brothers [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus]] and [[Markieff Morris]] left for the [[2011 NBA Draft|NBA draft]], he became a starter,{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/andy_glockner/04/02/Kansas.Jeff.Withey/index.html|title=Withey could be difference maker as Kansas looks to upset Kentucky |publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=April 2, 2012}} playing for the 2011-2012 squad which lost to Kentucky in the NCAA championship game. Withey blocked 31 shots in the 2012 tournament, breaking [[Joakim Noah]]'s tournament record of 29.{{cite web|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2012/04/02/3532103/no-joy-in-block-record-for-withey.html|title=No joy in block record for Withey|publisher=Kansas City Star|date=April 2, 2012}} During the 2011-12 season, he was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] defensive player of the year and set a Big 12 record with 140 blocks for the season. ==== 2012-2013 Season ==== On October 4, 2012, Withey was named to the Preseason [[Big 12 Conference|all-Big 12]] unanimously.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2012/oct/04/jeff-withey-named-preseason-all-big-12-elijah-john/?mens_basketball Jeff Withey named to preseason all-Big 12; Elijah Johnson honorable mention], Lawrence Journal-World, October 4, 2012. On December 3, 2012, Withey was named Big 12 Player of the Week. To earn the honor, he scored a [[triple-double]] against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State Spartans]] on November 26. In that game, Withey scored 16 points, grabbed 12 rebounds, and blocked 12 shots, for the second triple-double in KU history.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2012/dec/03/jeff-withey-wins-big-12-player-week/?mens_basketball Jeff Withey wins Big 12 player of week], [[Lawrence Journal-World]], December 3, 2012. On February 18, 2013, Withey was named Big 12 Co-Player of the Week. He had [[double-double]]s against both [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State Wildcats]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. He also made his 265th blocked shot to set a new Big 12 record for career blocked shots.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/feb/18/kansas-center-jeff-withey-shares-big-12-player-wee/?mens_basketball Kansas center Jeff Withey shares Big 12 player of the week honors], [[Lawrence Journal-World]], February 18, 2013. On March 10, 2013, he was named defensive player of the year in the Big 12 for 2012-13 and he was named first team All Big 12.{{Cite web | last = Bedore | first = Gary | title = Jeff Withey, Ben McLemore selected to All-Big 12 first team | url = http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/mar/10/kansas-center-jeff-withey-named-big-12-defensive-p/?mens_basketball | publisher = KUsports.com | date = March 10, 2013 | accessdate = 11 March 2013 }} On March 11, 2013, Withey was named 2nd Team [[All-American]] by The Sporting News.{{Cite web | last = Keeley | first = Laura | title = Seth Curry named Sporting News All-American | url = http://blogs.newsobserver.com/dukenow/seth-curry-all-american | publisher = newsobserver.com | date = March 11, 2013 | accessdate = 13 March 2013 }} On March 31, 2013, Withey was accorded third-team All-American mention by the [[Associated Press]].Bedore, Gary. [http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/apr/01/ben-mclemore-earns-second-team-ap-all-america-hono/?mens_basketball KU freshman Ben McLemore earns All-America honors], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', April 1, 2013 On April 5, 2013, the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] named Withey the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|co-National Defensive Player of the Year]]. ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/40989/jeff-withey *http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/withey_jeff00.html *http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Jeff-Withey-5259/ *http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/results/players?id=19763&_slug_=jeff-withey&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fnba%2fdraft%2fresults%2fplayers%3fid%3d19763%26_slug_%3djeff-withey *http://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/25/sports/ncaabasketball/jeff-withey-of-kansas-is-a-shot-blocker-supreme.html *http://www.huffingtonpost.com/jordan-schultz/kentucky-kansas-preview-matchups_b_1397305.html {{NABC Defensive Player of the Year}} {{2013 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Persondata | NAME = Withey, Jeff | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = March 7, 1990 | PLACE OF BIRTH = [[San Diego, California|San Diego]], [[California]], [[United States|U.S.]] | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Withey, Jeff}} [[Category:1990 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2012 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from California]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from San Diego, California]]
